macro_events.title: Microsoft Azure Crosses $100B Annual Revenue — Stock Gaps +15.5%
macro_events.causal_chain: Azure revenue grows 43% YoY → crosses $100B annually → validates hyperscaler AI capex thesis → second-order: partner ecosystem (CRM, NOW, ORCL) benefits from Azure workload growth → semiconductor demand pull-through (NVDA, AMD data center GPU orders) → institutional rotation into cloud winners from social/consumer tech → MSFT▲ CRM▲ NOW▲ AMZN▲ (sympathy) → counterpoint: $3.2B Anthropic investment gain flatters one-time EPS
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global cloud infrastructure, US tech sector
macro_events.historical_analog: AWS Q1 2019 inflection — Amazon cloud reaccelerated to 41% growth, stock rallied 25% over next quarter. MSFT's 43% mirrors that trajectory.
macro_events.counterargument: Revenue beat driven partly by one-time Anthropic gain; hyperscaler capex approaching $500B+ collectively, raising questions on sustaining marginal returns at scale.

affected_tickers.reason: Azure $100B, EPS $4.81 vs $4.24 est, cloud acceleration from 40% to 43%
AWS sympathy + own cloud acceleration reported; +3.9%

macro_events.title: Meta Q2 Earnings Miss — EPS $6.18 vs $7.22 Est, FCF Collapsed 91%
macro_events.causal_chain: Meta reports EPS miss of $1.04 → $2.4B legal charges + $1.18B severance → free cash flow crashes from $8.55B to $784M → capex guidance raised to $130-145B → market questions: spending $140B/yr on AI with no clear revenue attribution → institutional selling → second-order: social media peers (SNAP, PINS) face contagion on AI ROI skepticism → contrast with MSFT's clear monetization amplifies the gap → META▼ SNAP▼ PINS▼
macro_events.historical_analog: META Oct 2022 earnings — capex guidance shock sent stock -24% in one session. Current -8% is milder but the FCF collapse (91% drop) is actually worse.
macro_events.counterargument: Revenue still grew 28% YoY; $2.4B legal charges are one-time; AI infrastructure spending today seeds future monetization. Advertising market fundamentals remain strong.

affected_tickers.reason: EPS miss $6.18 vs $7.22; FCF collapsed 91%; capex raised
Social media contagion on AI ROI skepticism
Ad-tech peers dragged by META's miss
Ad market leader; benefits from META weakness but faces same AI capex questions

macro_events.title: Fed Holds at 3.50-3.75% — 3 Hawkish Dissents Push 30Y to 19-Year High
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed holds rates in 9-3 vote → 3 members wanted 25bp hike → signals internal division on inflation → 30Y yield surges to 5.24% (19-year high) → higher discount rate compresses long-duration equity valuations → mortgage rates rise further → housing activity slows → but bank NIM expands → next flashpoint: Aug 12 CPI → if hot, September hike odds spike → DXY firms near 100.8-100.9
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic, global bond markets, EM currencies
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2006 dissent pattern before final pause — 3 dissents preceded a 6-month hold period. Current parallel: hawks want more but data may not support it.
macro_events.counterargument: Core PCE trending lower at 3.3% (from higher levels); GDP miss suggests economy moderating naturally; August CPI could vindicate doves.

affected_tickers.reason: 30Y at 5.24% crushes long-duration bond prices
Utility yields unattractive vs 5%+ risk-free rate
Higher rates boost net interest margins
Rising mortgage rates pressure homebuilders

macro_events.title: Q2 GDP Misses at 1.5% vs 1.8% Estimate — Stagflation Whispers
macro_events.causal_chain: GDP 1.5% vs 1.8% est → growth decelerating while core PCE at 3.3% → stagflation signal (weak growth + sticky inflation) → defensive rotation: quality factor outperforms → consumer discretionary underperforms → staples/healthcare catch bid → counterargument: could accelerate rate cut timeline if growth slows further
macro_events.historical_analog: Q3 2022 GDP scare — initial miss triggered 5% drawdown before revised higher. Growth scares in tightening cycles tend to be buying opportunities if no recession follows.
macro_events.counterargument: GDP is backward-looking; ISM and PMI data may show forward recovery. Consumer spending remains resilient on services.

affected_tickers.reason: Defensive rotation into staples on growth scare
Consumer discretionary pressured by slowing economy
Healthcare catches defensive bid

macro_events.title: Iran/Hormuz Tensions — Oil Spike vs 3.7M bbl/day Oversupply
macro_events.causal_chain: US strikes on Iranian infrastructure + Strait of Hormuz shipping threats → war-risk premiums on VLCCs → Brent spiked to $80s but settled back to ~$72 → IEA projects 3.7-4.0M bbl/day oversupply from OPEC+ quota increases → net: geopolitical premium partially priced, oversupply caps sustained rally → XOM/CVX benefit as hedges → airlines (DAL) face fuel cost uncertainty
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, global oil markets, US energy sector
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq drone attack — Brent spiked 15% intraday then reversed within 2 weeks as supply concerns faded. Current situation: oversupply backdrop is worse than 2019.
macro_events.counterargument: OPEC+ adding 188K bbl/day in August caps upside; Russian production at 10.54M bbl/day is stable. Oversupply is the dominant force.

affected_tickers.reason: Energy hedge + uptrend intact + geopolitical premium
Integrated major benefits from crude volatility
Fuel cost risk offset by demand recovery

macro_events.title: China Section 301 Tariff — 12.5% on Forced-Labor Goods; Exports Surged 27%
macro_events.causal_chain: July 24 Section 301 tariff raises effective China rate to 23.4% → Chinese exports surged 27% YoY in June (front-loading before tariffs) → July/August imports likely to collapse as pipeline clears → semiconductor/electronics supply chain disruption risk → AAPL China consumer exposure a headwind → but front-loading means goods already in US pipeline → short-term inflationary pulse as tariff costs pass through
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 tariff escalation — front-loading surge followed by import cliff. ISM fell to 47.8 (contraction) within 2 months.
macro_events.counterargument: Overall tariff burden lower than 2019 peaks; supply chain diversification to Vietnam/India mitigates some impact.
